result:
Experiment design is written to `runs/pending_experiment.json`.

**Design summary:** After 20 straight reverted rounds sweeping nearly every decode family (VQ, GMM, dense-consensus, spatial MoE, retrieve-rerank, factorized axes) and every trunk-objective swap (contrastive, reconstruction, ShuffleNetV2, from-scratch, twin specialists), the one clear signal in the whole history is that the *only* trunk-only swap that kept the champion's field/decode untouched (exp-42, contrastive pretraining) landed closest to champion (846m vs 743m) — every experiment that also rewrote the decode landed far worse. That points at descriptor content, not decode shape, as the wall.

This round revives exp-38's idea — a fixed, non-learned Retinex-style illumination-invariant channel — which was never actually trained (rejected pre-implementation on compliance grounds only). It pairs a from-scratch trunk (mobilenet banned this round) with:
- a fixed geometric invariant channel targeting the previously-diagnosed blur/lighting-nuisance riding in the descriptor,
- deletion of the now-redundant two-expert bright/dark gate,
- a new cross-lighting descriptor-consistency loss (same location, two lighting buckets, pooled descriptors pulled together).

Every non-frozen stage is marked changed and tied to a real code diff, not just cosmetic dimension bumps — the implementation brief gives file-level instructions for `model/model.py` and `model/train.py` while preserving the ONNX export and CLI contracts. This is now handed off to the implementation stage.
